title: Bounds and summability for a nonnegative real sequence
statement:
Let $a:\mathbf N\to\mathbf R$ satisfy $a_n\ge0$ for every $n$. Here $\sum_n a_n$ is summable if the net $F\mapsto\sum_{n\in F}a_n$, over finite subsets $F\subset\mathbf N$ ordered by inclusion, converges to a real number.
(i) If $\sum_n a_n$ is summable with sum $A$, then $\sum_{n\in F}a_n\le A$ for every finite subset $F\subset\mathbf N$.
(ii) If there is $B\in\mathbf R$ such that $\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}a_n\le B$ for every $N\in\mathbf N$, then $\sum_n a_n$ is summable. Convergence is for the usual absolute-value metric $d(x,y)=|x-y|$ on $\mathbf R$, with absolute value as in [def-weil-complex-absolute-value].
